### 11.1 What the classification is worth

The category of a row is taken from a conventional-commit prefix when the subject carries one, and
from the files the commit touched when it does not. That makes the table readable and it makes the
history's own discipline measurable. Two typographic rules apply to the quoted subjects: a path
separator becomes a middle dot and a compound identifier keeps its parts in lower case. Wording and
word order are untouched, and a subject that names a file names it as it was written.
